jobs.description:
POSITION SUMMARY

The Workforce Strategy & Analytics team is looking for a Senior Manager to lead Customer Service & Operations (CSO) Demand Forecasting & Analytics.

The Senior Manager is responsible for identifying, shaping, and delivering strategic outcomes for the CSO organization through a variety of business analytics disciplines. This individual will collaborate closely with business leaders, serving as a thought partner and driving organizational decision making by leveraging data and analytical insights across multiple areas of the business.

This role specifically supports CSO, and the individual will consistently participate in strategic discussions with the Client leadership team, using their influence to help direct the organization’s strategy and address its most complex and high-priority challenges. An ideal candidate will be adept at making analytically sound decisions, even when information is limited, ensuring that solutions align with business priorities and support the overall goals of the organization.

This is a fully remote opportunity for candidates in select geographies. Candidates who reside within 50 miles of the following locations will be required to perform onsite 3 days per week: Bloomfield, CT; Chattanooga, TN; Denver, CO; Scottsdale, AZ.; St. Louis, MO.

Position Summary
- Responsible for providing strategy and analytics support for the Customer Service Operations team responsible for delivering customer service support across Medical, Dental, Digital, Chat and Pharmacy Benefit Services (PBS).
- Lead a team of business analysts and resource planning professionals, working closely with Operations, Workforce Management, Product and Technology teams to guide the development of analytical models/insights and build compelling business cases that positively influence the outcomes of the opportunities at hand.
- Maintain, improve and publish call volume, case volume and average handle time forecasts across multiple lines of business.
- Work closely with upstream and downstream Business, Finance and Operations partners to identify and size new pieces of intent and ensure these are accurately and timely captured to enable staffing strategies that optimize for both member experience and operational expenses.
- Act as a key thought partner for both the executive they support and their direct reports

Primary Components
- Leadership:  Recruit and sustain a high performing analytics team capable of providing exceptional analytics and strategic insights to their primary executive partner organizations in CSO . Individual will set an exceptionally high bar for excellence, coach current associates to their full potential and recruit / develop high potential talent into open roles. Individual will create a collaborative culture that has a high degree of ownership for their work product while providing exceptional support for their partner/customer organization in CSO.
- Strategy:  Using a background of proven business acumen, make analytically grounded strategic recommendations to key stakeholders across Operations, Workforce Management including Footprint, Product and Tech. The individual will think far beyond “tomorrow” to identify transformational opportunities for change. The individual will partner with the C&CE Strategy & Analytics team on our mid to long-term Data Strategy in the context of the strategic transformation that will enable the Workforce of the Future. The individual will l ead and/or support several strategic efforts such as Tech investments and deployment of AI capabilities in the C&CE ecosystem.
- Predictive modeling:  Maintain and improve forecast models by assessing new data elements, new drivers and modeling techniques, back-testing and validating the accuracy of these models.
- Analytics:  Employ a range of analytical techniques to assess the impact of new intent ( e.g. new clients, new products, new technology, OPEX initiatives), identify business opportunities and make strategic recommendations. The individual will identify the right series of analytics approaches for each individual situation, understand the strengths and weaknesses of the analysis or model, and effectively incorporate those into the overall recommendation. The individual will also look to influence the identification, testing and deployment of new intent. This may include supporting the development of business cases, providing guidance on test design and analytics as well as making recommendations on deployment timing and associated staffing strategy, balancing risk vs. rewards.
- Execution:  Publish call volume, chat volume and average handle time long-range and short-range forecasts across US Employer (USE) and PBS lines of business.  The individual will also monitor and analyze forecast variance for these LOBs, digging into drivers and assessing/monitoring the impact of new intent.

Key Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in Math, Economics, Statistics, Engineering, Business or related field preferred
- 5 years of relevant management consulting (preferred) or analytics experience
- Strong communication (oral and written) skills, including an ability to present work products to senior executives and influence buy-in
- Ability to lead large scale project and program teams and independently drive work forward
- Ability to partner across organizations and roles to influence and deliver work
- Two years of building, managing, or using business models, e.g. optimization, predictive analysis, or financial / credit modeling
- Strong analytical and finance skills are required – Proficiency in an analytics-focused coding language, e.g. SQL, Python, or R

Preferred Qualifications
- MBA or other relevant graduate degree in Math, Economics, Statistics, or Engineering
- 2+ years of people leadership experience
- Eight or more years of relevant analytics or management consulting experience
- Relevant healthcare experience
- Relevant experience in Operations and/or Customer Experience roles
- Four or more years of end-to-end model design and ownership experience, e.g. optimization, predictive analysis, or financial / credit modeling

jobs.title: Senior Principal, Enterprise Strategy & Strategic Opportunities
jobs.description:
The Senior Principal, Enterprise Strategy & Strategic Opportunities is a senior leader within Enterprise Strategy, Ventures & Innovation responsible for shaping and advancing high-value enterprise and business strategies. The role will own a portfolio of consequential opportunities and unresolved strategic questions, with primary focus on critical problem solving, business opportunities, and new growth and business innovation. The Senior Principal will turn broad, ambiguous questions into clear strategic choices, opportunity cases, and executive-ready recommendations that drive enterprise value.

The Senior Principal will also provide senior leadership capacity across the broader Enterprise Strategy agenda, including enterprise strategic positioning and competitive strategy and enterprise-choice work, long-term enterprise strategy and strategic priorities strategy development, and selected strategic planning priorities. The role will operate across enterprise trade-offs, portfolio implications, and cross-business opportunities, regularly engaging ELT members, business unit and corporate function and shared services leaders, and other senior stakeholders. Two positions may be hired against this common role profile, with portfolios flexed over time based on enterprise priorities, individual strengths, and demand.

This leader is expected to combine strong external orientation, strategic judgment, commercial insight, and the ability to lead through influence. The Senior Principal will autonomously drive major bodies of work, mobilize cross-functional teams, build trusted relationships across the enterprise, and serve as a thought partner to senior leadership on opportunities, risks, and new solutions.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic Opportunities & Critical Problem Solving
- Own a portfolio of the most important unresolved enterprise or business questions and convert broad asks into structured, decision-ready strategic options.

- Identify and evaluate growth opportunities, strategic adjacencies, partnerships, capability plays, and business development pathways that can create meaningful enterprise value.

- Lead rigorous problem framing, issue-tree development, strategic and economic analysis, scenario assessment, and recommendation development.

- Clarify enterprise trade-offs, value-creation logic, risks, dependencies, and execution requirements for senior leadership decisions.

- Mobilize and lead cross-functional teams and flexible strategy pods, maintaining pace, quality, and alignment from question definition through leadership decision.

New Growth and Business Innovation
- Shape new growth and business innovation strategies that create new growth, strengthen scaled core businesses, or evolve future business models.

- Identify opportunities where new propositions, channels, partnerships, technologies, capabilities, or combinations of enterprise assets can improve customer value, economics, growth, or long-term advantage.

- Develop innovation and opportunity theses, future-state models, growth platforms, and incubation or investment logic.

- Partner with business units, innovation, Corporate Development, Finance, and enterprise leaders to pressure-test concepts, build opportunity cases, and determine which ideas merit further investment or action.

- Move beyond idea identification by defining the strategic path, critical choices, evidence requirements, and early actions needed to advance priority opportunities.

Enterprise Strategic Positioning, Long-Term Strategy & Enterprise Direction Support
- Lead or support high-consequence enterprise strategic positioning and competitive strategy and enterprise-choice work involving where the enterprise plays, where value shifts, which moves matter, and what trade-offs leadership must make.

- Help steward and advance long-term enterprise strategy and strategic priorities by translating the enterprise direction into sharper choices, priorities, guardrails, growth hooks, and implications for businesses and corporate functions and shared services.

- Develop portfolio, pathway, competitive-position, and strategic-option analyses for Board and ELT discussions.

- Integrate external, customer, competitor, financial, and internal capability perspectives to challenge assumptions and strengthen enterprise recommendations.

- Partner with the VP of Enterprise Strategy and other senior strategy leaders on sensitive, confidential, and highly ambiguous priorities.

Strategic Planning & Cross-Team Leadership
- Provide senior strategy capacity to selected planning priorities, including challenging business strategies, testing strategic assumptions, and synthesizing implications across businesses and corporate functions and shared services.

- Partner with the Strategic Planning & Integration Lead to connect opportunity and innovation work to enterprise priorities, planning choices, and strategy-linked financial considerations.

- Contribute to enterprise planning reviews, leadership forums, and Board readiness where applied strategy expertise is required.

- Maintain durable ownership of assigned strategy lanes while deploying flexibly across the Enterprise Strategy portfolio as needs evolve.

- Help prioritize and deploy supporting talent across projects and develop Principals and Advisors through clear direction, coaching, and high-quality feedback.

External Insight, Relationships & Executive Influence
- Maintain a deeply external perspective on healthcare markets, customer and employer needs, competitors, policy, technology, capital flows, and emerging business models.

- Identify external developments that create enterprise opportunities, risks, strategic inflection points, or the need for new solutions.

- Build trusted relationships and an active network across business units, enterprise corporate functions and shared services, Corporate Development, Finance, innovation, peer groups, the Strategy Community, and senior leadership.

- Engage leaders to sharpen questions, surface diverse perspectives, create alignment, and improve the quality and speed of strategic decisions.

- Develop compelling executive narratives, presentations, and communications and represent Enterprise Strategy in leadership and cross-functional forums.

Qualifications
Required
- Bachelor's degree required; MBA or other relevant advanced degree strongly preferred.

- 10+ years of experience in corporate strategy, management consulting, business development, investment banking, private equity, innovation, or related strategic leadership roles.

- Demonstrated success leading enterprise-level strategy development, growth strategy, critical problem solving, or business opportunity work in complex organizations.

- Proven ability to autonomously lead ambiguous, high-consequence work and influence senior executives without direct authority.

- Exceptional strategic thinking, external orientation, commercial judgment, structured problem-solving, and executive communication skills.

- Strong analytical capabilities, including market and competitive assessment, business case development, financial analysis, scenario evaluation, and strategic synthesis.

- Experience mobilizing cross-functional teams and driving alignment across matrixed organizations.

- Proven ability to build broad, trusted relationships and navigate sensitive or confidential topics with sound judgment.

Preferred
- Experience in healthcare, health services, insurance, pharmacy, or adjacent industries.

- Experience in enterprise strategy, portfolio strategy, growth platforms, business model innovation, partnerships, or inorganic opportunity evaluation.

- Experience supporting Board, ELT, or comparable senior governance discussions.

- Demonstrated ability to develop talent and lead project teams across formal and informal reporting lines.

What Success Looks Like
- Enterprise and business leaders receive clear, differentiated, and decision-ready strategies on the most consequential opportunities and problems.

- New growth and business innovation priorities move from broad ideas to well-defined strategic choices, opportunity cases, and paths forward.

- Enterprise strategic positioning and competitive strategy, long-term enterprise strategy and strategic priorities, and planning work is strengthened by rigorous external insight, enterprise judgment, and clear articulation of trade-offs.

- The Senior Principal autonomously drives major work while creating meaningful leverage for the VP of Enterprise Strategy and other senior leaders.

jobs.title: Global Clinical Program Strategy Director - Cigna Healthcare - Hybrid
jobs.description:
The enterprise clinical team is reimagining its global talent model to support The Cigna Group’s Strategic Optimization Program (SOP). This program focuses on building clinical operations that are scalable, high quality, and efficient. The Principal, Global Talent Hub Clinical Lead, is responsible for turning the clinical global talent strategy into action. This includes building compliant clinical capabilities, transitioning roles based on regulatory and contract requirements, and delivering long-term value while maintaining quality, patient safety, and clinical integrity. This role offers a unique opportunity to help build a global clinical delivery model from the ground up and shape how clinical work is delivered safely and in compliance at scale. This position reports to the Managing Director, Enterprise Clinical Strategy and Operations.

Responsibilities
- Translate enterprise clinical global talent strategy into execution through structured, wave-based implementation plans that deliver measurable value across cost, quality, and scalability.

- Partner across Clinical, Enterprise Strategy, Global Talent, and external vendors to define and evolve the global clinical operating model, including scope such as utilization management, case management, pharmacy support, and administrative services.

- Lead clinical role assessment and governance processes to determine optimal role location, ensuring alignment with licensure requirements, regulatory standards, accreditation needs, and client contract obligations.

- Establish clear guardrails and scope boundaries by identifying which clinical roles are appropriate for globalization and documenting rationale to support decision-making and compliance reviews.

- Design and lead clinical transition planning, including vendor engagement, operating model selection (BPO, captive, or hybrid), and readiness assessments to support safe, compliant implementation.

- Ensure transition designs account for clinical-specific requirements such as credentialing, licensure, supervision structures, and enhanced quality and audit checkpoints.

- Build and scale global clinical and non-clinical teams by partnering with Talent Acquisition and HR to deliver recruiting, credentialing, and onboarding pipelines aligned to market supply and regulatory expectations.

- Establish clinical leadership models, including supervision layers and on-site leadership roles, to support safe delivery and clinical governance at scale.

- Implement end-to-end clinical process ownership with embedded quality metrics, productivity measures, service-level agreements, and patient safety indicators to ensure consistent outcomes.

- Ensure readiness for audits, accreditation, and client assurance processes, including data privacy, regulatory adherence, and quality performance standards.

- Design governance structures and value tracking methodologies that measure role transitions, cost-to-serve improvements, time-to-proficiency, and clinical quality outcomes.

- Proactively identify and escalate risks related to regulatory compliance, workforce readiness, and clinical quality, enabling timely resolution and continuous improvement.

- Drive stakeholder alignment and change management across clinical leaders, business units, Legal, Compliance, and Enterprise stakeholders to support successful global hub implementation.

- Develop and deliver executive-level communications and presentations that clearly articulate strategy, progress, and value realization of the clinical global talent model.

Qualifications
Required
- 8+ years of experience in healthcare, clinical operations, transformation, or delivery roles.

- Demonstrated experience leading or supporting global clinical delivery models, including GCC or GBS environments.

- Strong understanding of clinical regulatory frameworks, licensure requirements, and compliance standards.

- Proven ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives and end-to-end clinical transitions in dynamic environments.

- Experience working with core clinical functions such as utilization management, case management, or pharmacy support.

- Ability to balance competing priorities across cost, quality, speed, and regulatory considerations while driving decision-making.

Preferred
- 12+ years of experience in healthcare, clinical operations, transformation, or delivery roles.

- Experience supporting or building global clinical hubs in regions such as India or the Philippines.

- Familiarity with vendor delivery models, including BPO, captive, and hybrid operating structures.

- Understanding of clinical workforce economics, including productivity, attrition, and time-to-proficiency metrics.

- Experience developing partnerships with academic institutions, licensing bodies, or workforce pipeline programs.

About the Health Organization Department
Health Organization is a department created in 2026 and part of International Health Delivery Services. It encompasses Provider Network, Provider Operations, Payment Integrity, Clinical, Partnerships & Control and well as Strategy and Transformation.
Its mission is to drive provider excellence through smart network segmentation, outcome focused partnerships and shared accountability.
About the team & role
The Program Manager is empowered to drive strategic initiatives and deliver business transformation across the Provider Organization. He / she will be part of a very energetic and enthusiastic team leading innovative initiatives meant to exponentially transform the provider experience and internal operations.
The Program Manager is positioned to work hand in hand with a variety of teams and functions, spanning technology, finance, data and analytics operations etc. which offers he / she a unique perspective on business priorities, speed of execution new opportunities as well as challenges to overcome.
The role reports into the Head of Strategy and Transformation Director.
Responsibilities
- Lead and manage strategic projects from inception to completion, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and objectives.
- Collaborate with senior leadership and stakeholders to define project scope, deliverables, timelines, governance, business case and resource requirements.
- Develop and maintain comprehensive project plans, including schedules, budgets, risk assessments, and communication strategies.
- Monitor project progress, proactively identify and address risks or issues, and implement corrective actions as needed.
- Facilitate cross-functional collaboration, ensuring clear communication and coordination among internal teams, such as, D&A, Technology, PSO etc. and external partners.
- Prepare and deliver regular project updates, executive presentations, and post-implementation reviews.
- Analyse project outcomes, capture lessons learned, and recommend process improvements for future initiatives.

- Operational expertise: Experience or exposure in following functions: Claims, Pre-authorization, Network, Reconciliation, Strategy, Finance, Change management
- Strategic Thinking: Ability to see the big picture, connect dots across the organization, and translate strategy into actionable plans.
- Analytical Skills: Strong quantitative and qualitative analysis capabilities, with proficiency in data-driven decision making. Ability to evaluate and analyze information from a variety of sources
- Communication and Influence: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey complex ideas clearly

- Change Management: Experience supporting organizational change initiatives and guiding teams through transitions.

- Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with shifting priorities
- Energetic and enthusiastic team-player
- Ability to speak and write in languages other than English is preferred/but not required

Create the foundations to enable claims automation for Cigna International Healthcare in collaboration with architects, business process owners, agile delivery teams. - Rotate through a mix of technical depth assignments (data science, AI product, MLOps/platform, and AI product builder roles within our AI Innovation Office) and business-impact assignments (clinical analytics, affordability, customer experience, provider, and network analytics).
- Gain exposure to a range of working environments - from scaling analytics in established teams to contributing in fast-moving, R&D-style settings where new AI-powered products are rapidly prototyped and tested.
- Be paired with mentors, coaches, and sponsors empowering you to meet your goals and help you plan each next move.
- Move through a structured technical and leadership development experience designed to build both analytic capabilities and leadership skills.
- Build breadth and depth through rotations that prepare you for future analytics, AI, and product leadership roles.

- Identify matters requiring specialist legal, security or executive input and apply defined escalation protocols.

- Prepare dashboards, metrics and reports covering privacy operations, including rights requests, assessments, vendor reviews, incidents and operational KPIs.

Authority, accountability and escalation
- Represent the Chief International Privacy Officer within the scope of documented delegation, approved legal positions and applicable internal governance.

- Escalate significant incidents, enforcement risks, complex legal interpretations, potential material non-compliance and matters with cross-border or enterprise-wide impact.
